newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda continues to press for early debt relief.
newsitem.headline: Uganda continues to press for early debt relief.

text.p: Uganda is pressing for early debt relief from the World Bank and the IMF, and expects a decision by next month, finance ministry officials said on Wednesday.

The International Monetary Fund's executive board was due to meet in Washington later on Wednesday to discuss a plan to provide Uganda with up to $385 million of debt relief under a plan to help the world's most-indebted poor countries.
"We have been pressurising Washington to give us debt relief this year and the decision is to be taken in April," said Tumusiime Mutebile, permanent secretary in Uganda's finance ministry.
"We have been arguing that in our case we have had 10 years adjustment so we don't need another year (before relief is implemented)."
In general a country is expected to show a record of six years of economic reform under IMF tutorship before qualifying for major debt relief.
Monetary sources in Washington said on Tuesday that Britain favoured implementation of debt relief in the autumn while the United States was in favour of delay until April 1999.

Ugandan Finance Minister Jehoash Mayanja-Nkangi has said that a delay in implementation even to April next year, rather than in April this year, would mean that the effective debt relief would be cut in half.
Uganda, with a population of 21 million people, has external debts totalling $3.5 billion, of which $268 million is in arrears. Its per capita income was only $240 in 1995.

The finance ministry estimates that the equivalent of 60.2 percent of gross domestic product will be taken up by servicing debts in the financial year ending June, compared with 104.5 percent in 1991/1992.
The biggest creditor is the World Bank, whose International Development Agency is owed $1.82 billion, followed by the IMF, owed $422.9 million.
